🔐 Daily Security & Standards Brief (Nov 02)

Suggested IETF 127 Sessions for Getting Familiar with New Topics: worth a read if you ship against the spec.
CVE-2026-104935 — Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers: patch Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers and verify the fix held.
  ↳ Immediately apply the vendor patch for Ivanti Connect Secure to remediate predictable identifier generation and prevent session hijacking attacks
CVE-2026-104935 — Ivanti Connect Secure: enforce auth on the exposed function in Ivanti Connect Secure.
  ↳ Immediately apply the vendor-provided patch for Ivanti Connect Secure and restrict administrative interfaces to trusted networks only
CVE-2026-97229 — GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition Integer Overflow or Wraparound: patch GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition Integer Overflow or Wraparound and verify the fix held.
CVE-2026-76418 — Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference: patch Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference and verify the fix held.

That standard is what Blue-Team discipline is built on.

php2shell one week later: Why one exploit doesn’t work everywhere
top.summary: php2shell raised fears of mass exploitation. A week of testing by our research team found that working exploits had to be fitted to each target’s exact PHP setup. Systems that share one build, such as network appliances, are the exception: one tuned exploit can reach every device that runs it. Key takeaways The five vulnerable PHP sites we exposed to the internet were not compromised, and public proofs-of-concept (PoCs) that go beyond version checks do not reliably confirm whether a host is vulnerable. top.title: CVE-2026-118527 — Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers Vulnerability
top.summary: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357.

top.title: CVE-2026-111357 — Ivanti Connect Secure Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
top.summary: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.

top.title: CVE-2026-97229 — GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition Integer Overflow or Wraparound Vulnerability
top.summary: GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition contain a integer overflow or wraparound vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation.

top.title: CVE-2026-76418 — Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference Vulnerability
top.summary: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software contains an unchecked return value to NULL pointer dereference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

top.title: CVE-2026-41709 — Broadcom VMWare ESX Insufficient Logging Vulnerability
top.summary: Broadcom VMWare ESX contains an insufficient logging vulnerability that could allow a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.

top.title: CVE-2026-46300 — Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability
top.summary: Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root.

top.title: CVE-2026-48356 — Adobe Commerce and Magento Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability
top.summary: Adobe Commerce and Magento contain an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session.

top.title: CVE-2026-111497 — Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability
top.summary: Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.

top.title: CVE-2026-109618 — PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability
top.summary: PHP contains an out-of-memory corruption vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.

top.title: CVE-2026-109619 — PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability
top.summary: PHP contains a stale internal request-state vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.

top.title: OpenSSF Newsletter – October 2026

top.title: New LF Research Survey Shows Generative AI Cuts Open Source Coding Time in Half, but 25% of Incoming Pull Requests are Considered AI Slop
top.summary: While Generative AI boosts developer productivity and lowers barriers to entry, a new Linux Foundation Research report reveals it also increases maintainer workloads. With 25% of incoming pull requests now considered "AI slop," the findings highlight an urgent need for stronger open source project governance.

top.title: New OpenSSF Tech Talk: How Upstream Contribution Minimizes Technical Debt & Streamlines CRA Reporting
top.summary: Maintaining private forks of open source software (OSS) comes with a hidden tax, costing organizations an average of 5,160 labor hours per release cycle in maintenance and engineering overhead. Beyond the accumulating technical debt and security risks, passive open source consumption is no longer sustainable under emerging regulatory frameworks like the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), which imposes strict security and vulnerability management mandates.

top.title: Who Checked It? Attestations, Gemara, and CRA Due Diligence

top.title: New OpenSSF Guide: Finding and Fixing Vulnerabilities Using AI
top.summary: AI has gotten good at finding software vulnerabilities, and attackers are already using it. For example, “AI-enabled adversaries increased attacks by 89% year-over-year” according to the CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report. If you maintain or develop software, it is critical to find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them.
